title: fix(driver-sql,cli): a unique index its rows violate is listed as not appliable, never offered --allow-destructive
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wgULzXHHREefG78bonpN6vqt)_

Fixes #25031

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

Card thread of `domain:engine` seat 2 (seat post #20966), session `session_01YRXQdFH1TrCyDQ5L1xDQRg`, claim 6340150456. Cross-lane declaration for the one CLI line: comment 6340209215 on #22648.

## What changes

`driver-sql`'s ADR-0120 D4 duplicate pre-flight now declares a blocked unique index's apply limit **on the entry**: a new optional `ManagedDriftEntry.applyLimit`, set in the same branch that marks the entry BLOCKED, with the conflicting groups as the reason. The CLI's apply-limit seam (`SchemaStack.driftApplyLimit`, `schema-migrate.ts`) reads the entry's own limit first, then the owning driver's per-op one. One line of CLI code, as routing correction 6307307994 invited.

Nothing in `plan.ts` / `apply.ts` changes. The rendering PR #24954 and PR #25029 built for declared limits takes over: the entry is listed with its reason, the footer and the skip lines stop offering `--allow-destructive` for it, and it is counted among the changes that remain drift.

## Measured (SQLite file, rows duplicating a plain and an organization-scoped unique index)

| Door | `main` @ `e5f194b` | This branch |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `os migrate plan` | footer `Apply with: os migrate apply (add --allow-destructive for drops / tightenings)`, exit 0 | each entry ends `"os migrate apply" cannot apply it on this database: existing rows already violate the unique key: (code="A") × 2 rows.`; footer `Apply with: os migrate apply` and `2 change(s) above cannot be applied on this database …`, exit 0 |
| `os migrate apply --yes` | `2 destructive change(s) will be SKIPPED (re-run with --allow-destructive to include them).` and `Skipped 2 destructive change(s) (re-run …)`, exit 0 | `2 destructive change(s) remain drift that a re-run with --allow-destructive cannot apply on this database either` and `Skipped 2 … that a re-run could not apply on this database either`, exit 0 |
| `os migrate apply --allow-destructive --yes` | both named NOT applied, `PARTIAL apply`, exit 1 | listing carries the limit; both named NOT applied, `PARTIAL apply`, exit 1 (unchanged, see below) |
| re-run of `plan` | as the first row | as the first row of this column |

`driver-turso`, measured at the driver: on the local and the remote face alike the blocked `create_index` was `destructive` with BLOCKED in the message, no structured field, and `driftApplyLimit('create_index')` answered `null`. Both faces inherit the pre-flight (`detectTableDrift` → `applyNullSafeUniquePreflight`; the remote face overrides only the probe's statement), so both now carry `applyLimit`. `TursoDriver` is untouched and still answers by op type.

## Why a structured field rather than a widened `driftApplyLimit(entry)`

- **One judgement.** The pre-flight already decides the block on that entry. The field records that decision where it is made. A per-entry `driftApplyLimit` would still need the driver to remember it per entry (a field or a side table) and add a second door to the same fact.
- **Smaller published surface, no narrowing.** One optional key on an exported interface (`yes (widening)`, measured: `applyLimit` appears once in `packages/drivers/driver-sql/dist/index.d.ts`). Widening the parameter of `TursoDriver.driftApplyLimit(opType)`, which is published, would narrow it for every existing caller, and an older CLI calling a newer driver with an op-type string would read `.op` of a string.
- **Version skew is benign both ways.** An older CLI ignores the field and prints as before. A newer CLI over an older driver finds no field and asks by op type.
- `--json` documents now carry `applyLimit` on a blocked entry. That is an additive key, and no other entry gains it.

## Not changed, deliberately: the PARTIAL verdict under `--allow-destructive`

The seat's mechanism note expected `apply --allow-destructive` to stop ending PARTIAL on the blocked entry's account. It still does, exit 1. `apply.ts` documents that `notApplied`, PARTIAL and the exit code never read declared limits: an entry the operator confirmed and the driver did not apply makes the run PARTIAL, because the database still differs from its metadata. It is the same verdict the Turso REMOTE face gives a tightening (`apply.remote-face.integration.test.ts`). Excluding declared limits from PARTIAL would change the CLI's exit-code contract for both cases, which is the `domain:cli` lane's call and more than the one line this card carries. The new integration pin records today's verdict, so a later ruling flips one assertion. Raised in the report as an open question.

## Tests

- `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-25031-blocked-unique-apply-limit.test.ts` (new): plain and organization-scoped blocked entries carry `applyLimit` naming the conflicting group, and the apply skips them under `allowDestructive`. Controls: a duplicate-free unique index has no `applyLimit` and a plain apply creates it, and deduplicating withdraws the limit.
- `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-remote-drift-apply-limit.test.ts` (+1 describe): local and remote faces each declare the limit on the entry, while `driftApplyLimit('create_index')` stays `null`.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.blocked-unique-index.integration.test.ts` (new, integration tier): real boot, real `plan` / `apply` over a SQLite file. Each blocked entry lists its conflicting group as the limit. No line offers `--allow-destructive` in `plan`, `apply --yes` or `apply --allow-destructive --yes`, and the last still reports PARTIAL with exit 1. Control: duplicate-free unique indexes keep the unchanged footer, and a plain apply creates them.

Runs at `fa53728a8`: `driver-sql` vitest 232 files / 3752 passed, 12 files skipped; `driver-turso` 94 / 2485 passed; `cli --project unit` 324 / 4777 passed; the new integration file 4/4; `typecheck` green for all three packages.

**Ablation** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` deleting the `d.applyLimit = …` line, `driver-sql` rebuilt, `ablation-dist-preflight --absent` passing): the driver-sql pins went red (3 of 4: both pins plus the dedup control, which first asserts the limit), with the duplicate-free control green. The Turso pins went red (2 of 6), with the 4 pre-existing cases green. The CLI pins went red (3 of 4), with the control green. Restored: blob equals `HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty, `driver-sql` rebuilt, and the preflight marker is present again in `dist/`.

## Gates

`dispatch-gates --commands` derived 73 families at `fa53728a8`. 71 exited 0. `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` exited 3 on the shallow clone, then 0 after fetching its fixture commit. **NOT MEASURED locally:** `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` (exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET: they need the whole workspace built). CI runs both. `--ran` reconciliation: 73 derived, 71 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED. `check:driver-conformance`: OK, 55 covered cells, 0 DEBT, 0 exempt. No ledger file is touched.

## Acceptance notes

- The listing still places a blocked entry under `Destructive (requires --allow-destructive)`, because `renderPlan` groups by `category`. The entry's own line and the footer now say it cannot be applied. The heading is CLI rendering and was out of scope. The Turso REMOTE tightening reads the same way today.
- `category: 'destructive'` itself is unchanged. It is what keeps a plain apply, dev `autoMigrate: 'safe'` and the artifact boot gate from attempting the CREATE. Reclassifying it is a separate question, and this PR does not answer it.
- The tightening arm of the pre-flight (`recreate_index` with `tightenNullSafeOnly`) sets the same field in the same branch. Since ADR-0131 D1 made the organization key part plain, no fixture here reaches that arm, so it is covered by construction, not by a pin.
- Unrelated to this diff: on a database with a blocked unique index, the deferred boot's flush still tries the CREATE and logs `[sql-driver] cannot create unique index …` at every `os migrate apply`, as on `main`.
